title: Integrate Smart Routing with burst admission decisions (fallback + backpressure)
author: Elena Popov
description: Motivation: Dedicated burst capacity requires routing to consult the Burst Admission Controller before borrowing from shared burst pools, and to behave safely when burst is denied (protecting non-burst tenants + preserving determinism). This PR wires the routing/gateway path into the admission controller, adds deterministic policy evaluation inputs, and defines the fallback/backpressure behaviors for denied/timeout cases. Summary of behavior: For Dedicated tenants with burst enabled, routing computes a BurstContext (tenant_id, region, hw_class, baseline allocation id, requested_concurrency/requested_tokens estimate, priority tier) and calls the Burst Admission Controller synchronously at request admission time. If admitted, routing tags the request with the admission grant_id and burst_pool_id and routes to the burst pool endpoint group; if denied, routing falls back to baseline dedicated capacity when available (no pool borrowing) and otherwise applies backpressure (HTTP 429 with structured denial reason + Retry-After) rather than retrying across neighbors. Determinism: The admission request includes a stable request_key (derived from gateway request_id + model_route + tenant_id) and a policy_snapshot_hash from the control-plane config cache. Routing does not “shop around” across pools/regions/hardware classes. For the initial release, burst is strictly within-region and within hardware class. Failure modes: If the admission controller call times out or returns 5xx, routing treats it as a deny with reason=admission_unavailable and routes only to baseline dedicated capacity; if baseline is saturated, we backpressure with 503 (no burst) to avoid accidental neighbor impact. Observability: Adds routing-side counters and latency histograms for admission calls, denials by reason, and fallback usage, and propagates denial reason codes to the client error surface (aligned with pr-23795). Notes: This PR intentionally does not implement queueing-on-deny; the chosen semantics for v1 are immediate decision + client-driven retry using Retry-After guidance. Queueing can be revisited once we have stronger end-to-end SLO evidence and per-tenant buffering policies.

implementation_notes: Decision flow: 1) If tenant.burst.enabled=false => unchanged routing behavior. 2) If enabled and request fits baseline capacity => route baseline (no admission call). 3) If enabled and baseline indicates saturation risk => call admission controller with BurstContext. 4a) ADMIT => route to burst pool, attach grant_id, emit admitted metric. 4b) DENY (pool_saturated | tenant_cap_reached | cooldown_active | fleet_safety_cap | policy_disabled | admission_unavailable) => attempt baseline route if capacity signal says safe; otherwise return backpressure. Backpressure mapping: When deny reason is capacity-related we return HTTP 429 and include x-redwood-burst-denial-reason plus a Retry-After (seconds) when provided by the admission controller; for non-retriable denials (policy_disabled) we return 403. Timeout budget: admission controller call is capped at 35ms p99 target; routing uses 50ms hard timeout and does not retry. This is to prevent tail amplification. Safety: If routing detects inconsistent config (missing hw_class / region mapping) it disables burst path for the request and logs an error with tenant_id + config version, then routes baseline only.
review_conversation: Mina Haddad: Can we guarantee we won’t bounce between baseline and burst across retries and create nondeterministic user experience? Please clarify request_key / idempotency strategy.

Elena Popov (author): Added request_key based on gateway request_id + route + tenant_id, and ensured routing never tries multiple pools. Also added note that client retries should reuse Idempotency-Key; gateway already does this for streaming reconnects. Updated docs/internal/burst/routing-integration-notes.md.
Ravi Menon: I’m concerned about calling admission for every request. Can we skip when baseline has headroom? Also please ensure this doesn’t regress hosted routing path.

Elena Popov (author): Added fast-path: only call admission when baseline capacity signal indicates saturation risk (or when request explicitly opts into burst via header set by internal batch jobs). Hosted path is untouched; dedicated-only code paths are gated by tenant plan + deployment mode checks. Added unit tests to assert hosted route selector does not import burst client.
Ethan Park: Please align deny reason handling with the reason codes from pr-23795 and avoid introducing new strings here. Also what’s the behavior when policy snapshot is stale?

Elena Popov (author): Updated mapping to use the shared enum + string constants from pkg/burst/denial_reasons.go. For stale snapshot, routing includes policy_snapshot_hash; admission controller returns deny reason=config_mismatch with retry_after=0 and we fall back to baseline only. Added metric burst_config_mismatch_total.

Peter Holtz: 503 vs 429 semantics matter for paging and client retry storms. Suggest 429 for capacity denial; 503 only for internal unavailability. Also add a circuit-breaker on admission timeouts to avoid cascading.

Elena Popov (author): Updated as suggested: 429 for capacity/cooldown/caps; 503 only when admission is unavailable AND baseline also cannot serve. Added a simple local circuit breaker: if admission timeouts > 5% over 1m window, skip admission calls for 2m and route baseline-only (emit burst_admission_cb_open).
testing: Unit: dedicated_route_selector tests cover (a) baseline headroom => no admission call, (b) admit => burst route selected + grant_id propagated, (c) deny tenant_cap_reached => baseline fallback when safe, (d) deny pool_saturated + baseline saturated => 429 w/ reason and Retry-After, (e) admission timeout => baseline-only; if baseline saturated => 503. Integration: added fake admission controller to routing integration harness to validate end-to-end header propagation and error mapping in gateway. Manual: replayed staging traffic sample with burst disabled and verified routing decisions identical (hash compare of route targets).
rollout_plan: Behind feature flags: routing.burst_admission.enabled (default off) and routing.burst_admission.region_allowlist. Enable in staging for 1 tenant, then dogfood in us-east/h100. SRE to monitor burst_admission_latency_ms p95 and denial-rate dashboards before expanding allowlist. Rollback: flip flag to disable admission calls; routing returns to baseline-only behavior.
release_notes: Dedicated: Burst-enabled tenants now consult burst admission before borrowing capacity. When burst is denied, routing falls back to baseline when possible or returns structured backpressure (429) with denial reasons and retry hints.
